title: Promise Fulfilled
body:
Promise Fulfilled

Arjuna commanded Prince Uttara to drive the chariot towards the Sami tree near the cremation grounds. There, despite Uttara's fears that he was being forced to touch a decaying corpse, Arjuna instructed him to climb the branches and retrieve the leather bag. When the bag was opened, Uttara beheld weapons that shone like the sun, including the legendary Gandiva bow. Arjuna revealed his true identity to the amazed and trembling prince, explaining that the five brothers and Draupadi were the very ones serving in King Virata's court.
The touch of the Gandiva sent a surge of celestial courage through Uttara's heart. He took the reins as Arjuna donned his leather gauntlets and twanged the Gandiva, sending a resounding, thunderous echo across the plains of Matsya. Hearing the unmistakable sound, Drona turned to Bhishma and warned that the great archer Arjuna had arrived. Duryodhana was elated, declaring that if Arjuna was discovered before the end of the thirteenth year, the Pandavas would be bound by their pledge to return to the forest for another twelve years.
A fierce wordy warfare erupted among the Kuru leaders. Karna boasted that he would slay Arjuna single-handed, prompting a stern rebuke from Aswatthama. Drona's son reminded the assembly that the kingdom had been stolen by the fraudulent throw of the dice, not won by heroic deeds, and that the Gandiva would send forth sharp arrows, not numbers on a game board. Bhishma, the wise patriarch, intervened to restore order and perform a precise astronomical calculation. He declared that, according to the movements of the planets, the thirteen-year period of exile and living incognito had terminated the previous day, and that the Pandavas' pledge had been perfectly and honorably fulfilled.
Arjuna charged the Kaurava host, systematically bypassing his revered preceptors after saluting Drona and Bhishma by shooting arrows that fell gently at their feet. He routed the Kaurava army, recovered the royal cattle, and returned to the Matsya capital in triumph, allowing Prince Uttara to take the credit for the victory to protect their disguise until the final, formal unmasking.

मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् ।
हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ।।

Translation: "Working under My direction, this material energy brings into being all animate and inanimate forms. For this reason, the material world undergoes changes." — Verse Gita IX-10
